sources.entry: MQTTX - An elegant Cross-platform MQTT 5.0 desktop client.

summary.one_liner: MQTTX is an open-source, cross-platform MQTT 5.0 client toolbox from EMQ with a desktop app, a command-line client, and a browser-based web client for testing and troubleshooting MQTT and IoT applications.
summary.what_it_does: The desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux) provides a chat-style interface for multiple MQTT connections and subscriptions, with TCP, TLS, and WebSocket support and MQTT 3.1, 3.1.1, and 5.0. It includes payload encoding and decoding (JSON, Base64, Hex, CBOR, MsgPack, Protobuf and Avro schemas, GZIP decompression), scripts, timed publishing, and inspection tools such as a Topic Tree, Dashboard, Traffic Monitor, and Payload Inspector. The CLI offers conn, pub, and sub commands, benchmarks via bench, IoT data simulation via simulate, and stdin and pipe support for scripts and CI. The Web client lets you debug MQTT over WebSocket in a browser, with optional Docker self-hosting. The README also describes an AI assistant (MQTTX Agent) in the desktop app and an installable MQTTX CLI skill for AI agents.
use_cases: debug MQTT messages during IoT development
test and troubleshoot a broker connection
run MQTT benchmarks and load tests from the terminal
debug MQTT over WebSocket in a browser
decode Protobuf, Avro, or binary MQTT payloads
automate MQTT checks in shell scripts or CI
how_to_run: git clone git@github.com:emqx/MQTTX.git && cd MQTTX && nvm use && yarn install
notable: Three clients in one project: desktop GUI, CLI, and browser-based Web client
Built-in MQTTX Agent for natural-language operation of the desktop app, with approval-based actions
Protobuf and Avro schema support plus CBOR, MsgPack, and GZIP decoding
Import and export of connections as JSON, CSV, Excel, XML, or YAML
Free public test broker at broker.emqx.io
caveats: The MQTTX Agent sends conversations and tool results to the configured model provider, so secrets should not be entered in chat
The Web client requires wss:// when the page is served over HTTPS
Desktop development requires Node.js v22 as specified in .nvmrc
